youtube.title: "The First Fire in a Spacecraft May Well Be Fatal." A Year Later, Apollo 1 Burned
youtube.description:
In 1966, General Electric's Hilliard Paige warned that the first fire in a spacecraft may well be fatal. On 27 January 1967, during a routine test on the launch pad, a spark in Apollo 1's pure-oxygen cabin killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee. The inward-opening hatch could not be opened in time. NASA rebuilt the spacecraft, and Apollo 7 flew 21 months later.

📂 Case File #042: The Apollo 1 Warning
